subject: Discovery recap: ClearWell LLM API decoupling & POC next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@clearwell.ai>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@clearwell.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Discovery recap: ClearWell LLM API decoupling & POC next steps

Hi Oliver / Claire —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can move to a scoped POC: 

Key pain points you called out:
- Vendor lock: heavy dependency on OpenAI + Anthropic for generation + embeddings; concern about sudden API changes and pricing shocks.
- Unit cost: current monthly bill ~3M tokens + ~400k embedding calls; top line token spend has grown 4x year-over-year.
- Latency & throughput: occasional spikes causing degraded UX during peak ingestion windows (search/semantic-relevance flows).
- Compliance: handling PHI in search logs and needing stronger audit trails + encryption controls.

Current stack (we discussed):
- Production: OpenAI (chat/completions), Anthropic (instruct flows) for a mix of summarization, search re-rank, and assistants.
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (embedding dim 3,072) for vector search (Pinecone).
- Orchestration: in-house gateway that does token budgeting and simple retries.

Success criteria you listed (measurable):
1) Feature parity for our three primary flows (assistants, summarization, embedding-based search) within POC scope.
2) Cost reduction target: expected 30–45% decrease in per-unit inference cost at scale.
3) Ops & security: SOC2-level auditability, KMS integration, and data retention controls.
4) Latency/headroom: P95 < 800ms for 64-token assistant prompts and ability to handle 120 concurrent inference streams during peak.

Preliminary model shortlist (compatibility-minded):
- Llama-3-family (70B / 13B) — for generation and tool/function parity testing
- Mistral-Instruct (reliability on instruction prompts)
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (fast decode paths for summarization)
- Open-embeddings-compatible models (to match your 3,072-dim vectors) — we’ll validate dims/normalize as part of POC

Immediate next steps we proposed: 
- You to confirm stakeholders and compliance owner for a short intake (Claire / Security).
- We send a POC scope doc (attached: redwood_poc_plan.pdf) with success metrics, resource needs, and a 4-week timeline.
- You share the usage CSV and a sanitized sample payload (attached: clearwell_usage_summary.csv).
- Kickoff target weeks: Oct 25 or Nov 1 — please confirm preferred week.

Attachments included: clearwell_usage_summary.csv, security_questionnaire_signed.pdf, redwood_poc_plan.pdf, mvp_migration_timeline.xlsx

Open ask for you now: can you confirm (1) whether PHI is present in the payloads we’ll test for the POC and (2) which week you prefer for kickoff?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scoped.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@clearwell.ai>

Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 18:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: ClearWell LLM API decoupling & POC next steps

Thanks Evelyn — this is great, and captures it well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PHI: yes, some of our search logs ingest PHI (clinical notes redacted in the UI but present in text). That’s why SOC2 + HIPAA alignment is non-negotiable for production; for the POC we can provide sanitized samples, but we’ll need to validate KMS & audit logs before any live PHI flows.
- Volume: FYI our 3M tokens/month is a current-average; during trials (product beta) this spikes to ~6M tokens/month and concurrency can hit ~180 concurrent short calls for the assistant product for ~10–20 minutes during batch runs.
- Embedding dims: the 3,072-dim value is correct today. We are open to re-indexing if needed but would prefer to avoid a costly re-embedding job if possible.

Stakeholders to loop in: Alicia Park (VP Engineering), Samir Reddy (CTO), and our security lead Claire (cc’d). Alicia will want to see the proposed cost model and margin impact.

We prefer the week of Nov 1 for kickoff — gives us two weeks to complete an internal security intake.

Two quick asks for the team: 
1) Can you map the embedding compatibility approach (re-dimension vs. crosswalk vs. on-the-fly projection) in the POC doc?
2) Please include a fallback plan in case function-calling parity is not achieved in week 1.

Oliver

Head of Product | ClearWell
oliver.grant@clearwell.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

Hi Oliver / team —

Thanks for the details, Oliver. A few technical notes and how we’d structure the POC from an engineering/compatibility perspective: 

Technical approach (high level):
- Embeddings: we’ll include two tracks in the POC: (A) projection/crosswalk layer that maps your 3072-dim vectors into our candidate model embedding space (so you can avoid a full re-index), and (B) a re-embed & reindex path to validate quality delta. We’ll measure recall@10 and avg distance shifts as an explicit success metric.
- Tokenization & function-calling parity: we’ll test on a canonical prompt set to validate deterministic tokenization and function-call behavior. For functions, we provide a shim that translates your current function schema to the model-specific output fields to reduce integration work.
- Costs & quantization: for throughput flows we recommend running quantized variants (int8/4) and measuring quality drop. Our POC plan includes a small batch of perf runs to estimate per-1000-token cost at current concurrency.
- Security ops: KMS integration, customer-managed key option, and per-request audit logs are part of our Dedicated and Private offerings; we’ll include an audit-log sample for Claire to review.

POC scope (deliverables):
1) Week 0: sandbox setup + ingest sanitized payloads.
2) Week 1: model parity tests (generation + function calling) on canonical prompts.
3) Week 2: embedding compatibility tests (crosswalk vs re-embed) + recall metrics.
4) Week 3: perf load test at target concurrency and cost estimate.
5) Week 4: handoff, runbook, and ops checklist (KMS, retention, SLA notes).

We’ve attached a concise POC plan (redwood_poc_plan.pdf) and a suggested migration timeline (mvp_migration_timeline.xlsx). If you can share sanitized sample payloads and a short list of critical prompts (3–5) we’ll prioritize those in week 1.

A couple of questions for planning:
- Do you have any sinks that must remain real-time (sub-300ms) vs. best-effort (<=1s)?
- Will you require on-prem deployment for the pilot, or is a VPC-hosted private deployment acceptable for initial testing?

Happy to jump on a quick 30-min tech scoping call with Alicia / Samir if that helps.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
